title: OneDrive and SharePoint: external sharing moves to Microsoft Entra B2B guest accounts
summary: The briefing's rollout, access-restoration steps, licensing model and control paths are supported by Microsoft documentation. Minor corrections should remove the already-answered billing question and acknowledge checklist controls missing from the table.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans to replace SharePoint OTP with Microsoft Entra B2B invitation and authentication for OneDrive and SharePoint external users.
claims.quote: OneDrive and SharePoint will use Microsoft Entra B2B as the invitation and authentication method for external users, replacing the legacy SharePoint One Time Passcode (SPO OTP) experience.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: External sharing will automatically create B2B guest accounts in the directory, subject to the invitation restrictions described elsewhere in the briefing.
claims.quote: External sharing will automatically create B2B guest accounts in your directory

claims.where: front matter: status; What's changing; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.claim: The roadmap target is April CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "April CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap preview date is May CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "May CY2026"

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant), GCC, GCC High and DoD.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)", "GCC", "GCC High", "DoD"]

claims.where: front matter: platforms; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap platform is Web.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.claim: The roadmap lists General Availability, Preview and Targeted Release.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview", "Targeted Release"]

claims.claim: Microsoft enabled the integration for new external sharing in commercial tenants between May and July 2026.
claims.quote: Between May and July 2026, Microsoft enabled SharePoint and OneDrive integration with Microsoft Entra B2B for new external sharing in commercial tenants.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[2].note; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: EnableAzureADB2BIntegration no longer controls sharing behaviour in commercial tenants.
claims.quote: The EnableAzureADB2BIntegration setting no longer controls sharing behavior for these tenants, and the integration can't be disabled.

claims.claim: Commercial tenants cannot disable the integration.
claims.quote: Microsoft Entra B2B integration can't be disabled in commercial tenants.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Scope; changes
claims.claim: Microsoft documents SharePoint OTP retirement for commercial tenants starting in October 2026, with the FAQ specifying rollout during October 2026.
claims.quote: SharePoint Online (SPO) one-time passcode (OTP) authentication will be retired for commercial tenants during October 2026.

claims.claim: Microsoft Entra B2B email one-time passcode remains supported.
claims.quote: Microsoft Entra B2B email one-time passcode authentication remains supported.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Scope
claims.claim: A matching Entra B2B guest account allows external users to retain access to previously shared Specific people links after retirement.
claims.quote: When SharePoint OTP retirement reaches your tenant, external users need a matching Microsoft Entra B2B guest account in your directory to access previously shared Specific people links. Users with a matching guest account retain access.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: External users without a matching guest account receive access denied on previously shared Specific people links once retirement reaches the commercial tenant.
claims.quote: Once SharePoint OTP retirement reaches your commercial tenant during October 2026, users without a matching guest account receive access denied on previously shared Specific people links.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout; rationale: risk
claims.claim: An administrator can create the matching guest account using the original sharing link's email address, including proactively.
claims.quote: Yes. You can create a Microsoft Entra B2B guest account in advance using the email address associated with the original sharing link. A matching guest account lets the user retain access to previously shared content without resharing.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: A user with sharing permission can share or reshare one file, folder or site to create the account and restore access without resharing every item.
claims.quote: Alternatively, a user with sharing permissions can share or reshare at least one file, folder, or site with the external user. This automatically creates the guest account in Microsoft Entra B2B.

claims.claim: Tenants are selected automatically for retirement and administrators cannot choose a specific date.
claims.quote: Tenants are selected automatically, and you can't choose a specific date.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Scope
claims.claim: Anyone/Anonymous links are unaffected.
claims.quote: No, SPO OTP retirement and use of Entra B2B for external sharing does not impact Anyone/Anonymous links.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Invited external people receive directory accounts subject to Entra ID access policies such as multifactor authentication.
claims.quote: Invited people outside your organization each get an account in the directory and are subject to Microsoft Entra ID access policies such as multifactor authentication.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Entra organizational relationship settings, including Members can invite and Guests can invite, apply to SharePoint and OneDrive sharing as they do to Teams and Microsoft 365 Groups.
claims.quote: SharePoint and OneDrive sharing is subject to the Microsoft Entra organizational relationships settings, such as Members can invite and Guests can invite. As with Microsoft 365 Groups and Teams

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Entra setting prevails when more restrictive than the SharePoint or OneDrive setting.
claims.quote: if a Microsoft Entra organizational relationship setting is more restrictive than a SharePoint or OneDrive setting, the Microsoft Entra setting prevails.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Enabling the integration leaves SharePoint sharing settings unchanged, including sites where external sharing is off.
claims.quote: Enabling this integration doesn't change your sharing settings. For example, if you have site collections where external sharing is turned off, it remains off.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance controls; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Commercial tenants cannot opt out of SharePoint OTP retirement.
claims.quote: No. Commercial tenants can't opt out of SharePoint OTP retirement or disable Microsoft Entra B2B integration for new external sharing.

claims.claim: A duplicate guest account is not created when a collaborator already has one.
claims.quote: If a Microsoft Entra B2B guest account already exists for a collaborator outside your organization, a duplicate is not created.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Scope; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The change applies tenant-wide and cannot be scoped to individual sites.
claims.quote: No. The change applies at the tenant level and can't be scoped to individual sites.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Microsoft does not offer exceptions to this change.
claims.quote: 6. Can exceptions be made to this change? Answer: No. This update is part of Microsoft's ongoing efforts to enhance security.

claims.claim: The recipient-experience comparison documents Conditional Access for guest accounts but not ad hoc external recipients.
claims.quote: | | Guest account | Ad hoc external recipient | ... | Access controlled by Microsoft Entra Conditional Access policies | Yes | No |

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft advises reviewing custom SharePoint and OneDrive domain restrictions for possible migration to the Entra B2B Allow/Deny list, which also affects Teams and Microsoft 365 Groups.
claims.quote: Review any custom domain sharing restrictions in SharePoint and OneDrive and decide if they should be moved to the Microsoft Entra B2B Allow/Deny list. The Microsoft Entra ID Allow/Deny list also affects other Microsoft 365 services like Teams and Microsoft 365 Groups.

claims.claim: Guest invitation settings are in Microsoft Entra admin center > Entra ID > External Identities > External collaboration settings > Guest invite settings.
claims.quote: Browse to Entra ID > External Identities > External collaboration settings. ... Under Guest invite settings, choose the appropriate settings:

claims.claim: PATCH /v1.0/policies/authorizationPolicy sets who can invite external users through allowInvitesFrom.
claims.quote: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/policies/authorizationPolicy ... allowInvitesFrom ... Indicates who can invite external users to the organization.

claims.claim: Portal external collaboration settings require a role such as Global Administrator or External Identity Provider Administrator.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft Entra admin center, you need a role that can update external collaboration settings, such as Global Administrator or External Identity Provider Administrator.

claims.claim: Microsoft lists Privileged Role Administrator as the least privileged role for the authorizationPolicy update.
claims.quote: For delegated access using work or school accounts ... Privileged Role Administrator is the least privileged role supported for this operation.

claims.claim: The portal route for inviting a guest is Microsoft Entra ID > Users > New user > Invite external user.
claims.quote: Browse to Microsoft Entra ID > Users. ... Select New user > Invite external user from the menu.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/invitations creates an invitation and a B2B guest user.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/invitations ... When the user is invited, a user entity (of userType Guest) is created and can be used to control access to resources.

claims.claim: The cited portal procedure specifies at least User Administrator to invite guest users.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center as at least a User Administrator.

claims.claim: The portal invitation procedure automatically sends an invitation email.
claims.quote: An email invitation is automatically sent to the user. After you send the invitation, the user account is automatically added to the directory as a guest.

claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant -EnableAzureADB2BIntegration $true enables the integration where that legacy setting still controls it.
claims.quote: The following procedure applies only to tenants where the EnableAzureADB2BIntegration setting still controls the integration. ... Set-SPOTenant -EnableAzureADB2BIntegration $true

claims.claim: The integration procedure requires SharePoint Administrator permissions or higher.
claims.quote: Connect to SharePoint with permissions of a SharePoint Administrator or more in Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no SharePoint admin center UI setting for the integration at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint Entra B2B integration EnableAzureADB2BIntegration admin center UI setting. Opened sharepoint/sharepoint-azureb2b-integration and FAQ; examined search results for turn-external-sharing-on-or-off. The documented integration switch is PowerShell, not a portal control.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: The default state is on: the commercial-tenant change reaches users without administrator enablement.
claims.quote: Integration is already enabled for new external sharing in commercial tenants. ... Commercial tenants can't opt out of SharePoint OTP retirement

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Consumption is the documented guest licensing model because External ID MAU billing covers B2B collaboration guests in workforce tenants.
claims.quote: The MAU billing model for External ID applies to all guest users. Guest users include: External guests for B2B collaboration in Microsoft Entra workforce tenants.

claims.claim: MAU counts unique external users authenticating within a calendar month.
claims.quote: The basic External ID billing model is based on monthly active users (MAU), which is the count of unique external users who authenticate to your tenants within a calendar month.

claims.claim: The MAU billing model offers a free tier.
claims.quote: MAU billing helps reduce your costs by offering a free tier and flexible, predictable pricing.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The billing overview directs readers to the External ID pricing page for current rates.
claims.quote: For the latest pricing details, see External ID pricing.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Workforce tenants must be linked to an Azure subscription for proper billing and feature access.
claims.quote: Microsoft Entra workforce tenants must be linked to an Azure subscription for proper billing and access to features.

claims.claim: Linked subscriptions are under Microsoft Entra admin center > Entra ID > External Identities > Overview > Subscriptions > Linked subscriptions.
claims.quote: Go to Entra ID > External Identities > Overview. ... Under Subscriptions, select Linked subscriptions.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The SharePoint integration page itself names no licence or meter for the integration.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint OneDrive Entra B2B integration licensing meter guest MAU billing. Opened the SharePoint integration page, its FAQ and External ID pricing and billing overview; the SharePoint pages contain no integration-specific licence or meter.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Open questions: guest MAU counting
claims.claim: The SharePoint pages do not separately state whether sharing-created guests are counted differently from other B2B guests.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint OneDrive Entra B2B integration licensing meter guest MAU billing. Read the integration page and FAQ: neither discusses MAU. The External ID billing overview expressly covers all B2B collaboration guests in workforce tenants.
claims.fix: Remove the final Open questions bullet beginning 'Are guests created by SharePoint sharing counted as monthly active users'. The cited https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/external-id/external-identities-pricing already says the MAU model applies to all guest users, including B2B guests in workforce tenants; retain that established rule in Cost and licensing.

claims.claim: The integration page and FAQ give dates for commercial tenants without specifying the GCC, GCC High or DoD transition schedule.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint Entra B2B integration GCC GCC High DoD rollout retirement commercial 2026. Read integration page and FAQ and government-cloud search excerpts; no government OTP-retirement schedule was stated. The feature pages qualify the dates as commercial.

claims.where: Why it matters; Open questions: retirement indicator
claims.claim: Learn supplies no indicator to tell an administrator precisely when OTP retirement has reached their commercial tenant.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint OTP retirement how to tell tenant retirement reached indicator status. Read integration FAQ and retirement FAQ. Automatic selection is documented, but no retirement-status indicator; Get-SPOTenant is explicitly not authoritative for commercial integration enablement.

claims.claim: On a SharePoint site the report route is Settings > Site usage > Shared with external users > Run report.
claims.quote: Open the site where you want to run the report. ... On the Settings menu, select Site usage. ... In the Shared with external users section, select Run report.

claims.claim: Site administrators can run the external sharing report.
claims.quote: You must be a site admin to run the report.

claims.claim: The FAQ directs administrators to the report's User E-mail column to identify SPO OTP guests without B2B guest accounts.
claims.quote: At site level, use the external sharing report to get a list of guests invited via SPO OTP who do not yet have a Microsoft Entra B2B guest account. Refer to the "User E-mail" column.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends audit logs as a way to assess this change's impact.
claims.quote: Is there a way to report which previously shared links and external users are affected? Answer: Yes. You can use audit logs to assess the impact.

claims.claim: A B2B collaboration sign-in produces a sign-in log in the resource tenant.
claims.quote: When a B2B user signs into a resource tenant to collaborate, a sign-in log is generated in both the home tenant and the resource tenant.

claims.claim: Tenant-wide invitation domain restrictions are under Entra ID > External Identities > External collaboration settings > Collaboration restrictions.
claims.quote: Browse to Entra ID > External Identities > External collaboration settings. ... Under Collaboration restrictions, you can choose whether to allow or deny invitations to the domains you specify

claims.where: Governance guidance versus Governance controls table
claims.claim: Every control the governance checklist asks readers to review or use is represented in the controls table.
claims.quote: Ask site admins to run the external sharing report ... Use sharing audit records ... Review guest sign-in logs ... confirm the tenant is linked to an Azure subscription. The table covers guest invite settings, guest creation and the legacy integration switch.
claims.fix: The checklist's external sharing report, domain restriction review, sharing audit records, guest sign-in logs and linked Azure subscription check have no corresponding controls-table rows. This is a checklist/table coverage gap, not an incorrect path or command.

claims.claim: Variable cost correctly describes the documented MAU-metered External ID guest billing model.
claims.quote: External ID uses a basic monthly active users (MAU) billing model with optional premium add-ons for advanced scenarios.
